newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Infrastructure in A$143 mln motorway deal.
newsitem.headline: Infrastructure in A$143 mln motorway deal.

text.p: The Infrastructure Trust of Australia said on Monday it had committed to invest A$143.1 million in the Airport Motorway, a consortium which has the concession to build and operate the the Eastern Distributor tollway project in Sydney for 48 years.
The Trust said it had invested A$71.55 million today with the balance to be invested in 12 months time.
Infrastructure Trust holds 73.4 percent of Airport Motorway.
Other other investors comprise a unit of developer and contractor Leighton Holdings with 16.6 percent and funds manager Unisuper Ltd with 10 percent.
Infrastructure Trust securities ended three cents lower at A$1.32 on turnover of 428,098 shares.
The Trust said the cost of the Eastern Distributor project had escalated to A$565.6 million from A$400 million due to modifications after governmental environmental and public consultation processes.
Construction of the project is expected to commence in the next few days and was scheduled to be open for traffic in time for the Sydney Olympics in 2000, the Trust said.

Key differences from the prospectus forecasts and assumptions include an actual concession period of 48 years versus an original 38 years, and a toll of A$3 for cars and A$6 for trucks versus original figures of A$2 and A$4 respectively.
